doc.title: Frank Foster — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Larry Blaine's musical and the hipsters' stage ambitions
summary: Detroit fans wanted to take bebop beyond joints; Larry Blaine staged a musical for which Foster wrote background music.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Definitely, but the point I’m trying to make is, there were other people who had other ideas for culturally expanding the genre, people who wanted to give stage shows, stage presentations, who wanted to feature bebop musicians in stage plays and musicals. There was a guy named Larry Blaine who was a singer in a Billy Eckstine tradition. He had visions of putting on musicals.

He actually organized this musical. It featured a bunch of us young musicians. We had singers. We had dancers. We had -- I wrote -- he wrote a script, and I wrote background music. What I am trying to say is there were people who loved the music and wanted to culturally expand the image beyond just playing --
In joints, right. To bring it to concert stage and colleges or local auditoriums or whatever.
Can you think of other examples -­
And this didn’t happen in Cincinnati -- huh?
Can you think of other examples of that kind of activity that either you participated in or knew about?
No I can’t think of other examples. It is certain that it has been thought about in New York, but there was always lack of funds.
